🕵️‍♂️“The Definitive Guide to Epstein/Trump”🔍
🫆Copy/paste this into your favorite search engine and ask it to “please grade this for accuracy without innuendo”. 
You’ll get A+ across the board. 👍🏻

1: Donald Trump banned Jeffrey Epstein from Mar-a-Lago. Former Palm Beach Police Chief Michael Reiter testified that Trump contacted him during the Epstein investigation in June 2006 and praised police for going after Epstein, identified Ghislaine Maxwell as someone investigators should focus on, called her “evil,” and encouraged law enforcement to keep pursuing the case. 

2: When Epstein victims’ attorney Brad Edwards wanted information from Trump in 2009, Trump cooperated. Edwards said Trump was helpful, provided useful information, and was willing to sit for a deposition.

3: Virginia Giuffre, one of Epstein’s most prominent victims, testified: “I don’t think Donald Trump participated in anything.” She said she never saw Trump participate in Epstein’s abuse and specifically denied that Trump had ever flirted with her.

4: ABC News anchor Linsey Davis interviewed seven Epstein survivors together and directly raised Donald Trump with them. The women said they had no personal experience of being abused by Trump. Their attorney, Brad Edwards, reinforced the point: “Not a single victim has ever said he abused.” Anouska De Georgiou, who had actually been introduced to Trump by Ghislaine Maxwell, added that there was “no impropriety on the part of President Trump.”

5: Epstein’s own defense lawyers were also repeatedly questioned about Trump. Alan Dershowitz said he personally asked Epstein whether he had damaging information about Trump, and Epstein told him there was nothing. Jack Goldberger’s correspondence documented Trump voluntarily speaking with Brad Edwards rather than forcing him to pursue a deposition. Other Epstein attorneys, including Roy Black, Gerald Lefcourt, Jay Lefkowitz, Kenneth Starr, Guy Lewis, Lilly Ann Sanchez and others, handled Epstein’s case while Trump’s relationship with Epstein was being scrutinized, and none of those lawyers said that Trump participated in Epstein’s sexual abuse.

6: Trump knew Epstein socially. That is not disputed. But the victims, their attorney, Epstein’s own lawyers, and the former police chief who investigated Epstein tell a very different story from the accusation being spread online.

DOJ ACTIONS:
2008-2016 Obama DOJ: Brought no new federal prosecution of Epstein and made no comparable mass public release of Epstein investigative files.

Trump first-term DOJ: Arrested and federally charged Epstein in 2019 with sex trafficking of minors; roughly 2,000 pages of related court records were also unsealed in 2019.

Biden DOJ: Prosecuted Ghislaine Maxwell to conviction and a 20-year sentence. A 2024 court-ordered release of roughly 250 documents, and the Biden DOJ released about 950 pages.

Trump second-term DOJ: Beginning in 2025, DOJ undertook the first enormous government-wide public release, culminating in nearly 3.5 million pages released by January 2026. 
 * Of the remainder, the vast majority consists of duplicates or unrelated/nonresponsive material; about 200,000 pages from Epstein’s files were withheld or redacted for legal privilege, including child abuse images with additional redactions protecting victims, illegal sexual-abuse material, and legitimate investigative interests.

They have nothing to do with Trump but democrats weaponized these 200,000 files — even though they know these files are not meant for public humiliation of sexual assault victims. And their sheep became parrots.

Trump and Epstein were wealthy neighbors who moved in overlapping Palm Beach and New York social circles from the late 1980s into the early 2000s. Trump appears repeatedly in the Epstein files largely because he and Epstein belonged to the same Palm Beach/New York social circles for decades.

Independent indexes give a sense of scale: one current public-figure database tracks 365 public figures appearing in the released Epstein material, while broader searchable archives contain tens of thousands of distinct names overall. 

Epstein attended events at Mar-a-Lago, they were photographed together, Trump flew on Epstein’s plane on some domestic trips, and Epstein’s address book contained numerous Trump-related contact numbers. That naturally generates a lot of mentions in correspondence, flight records, photographs, witness interviews and investigative files. 

Many people appear simply because Epstein cultivated an enormous network of wealthy, famous and politically connected Miami and Manhattan acquaintances.

When talking about “The Epstein Files,” the better mental picture is a warehouse full of overlapping folders, not one spy-novel dossier titled “Everyone Who Did Something Wrong”.
